learning: Request telemetry on completion, progress, rms_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to verify if the smaller forward sensor shift improves line anticipation and control smoothness. Also monitor if line loss events decrease and progress increases, confirming improved robustness and stability. These measurements will guide whether further fine-tuning of sensor y-positions or other geometry changes are needed.
rationale: The previous iteration's telemetry shows persistent line loss events and off-track terminations despite improvements from moving sensors forward by +0.01 in y, increasing sensor size to 0.016, and wheel track to 0.16. The line loss events and steering oscillations remain, indicating the robot still struggles with early line detection and smooth control. To address this, I have fine-tuned the sensor y-positions by shifting them forward an additional +0.005 in y, aiming to detect the line slightly earlier and improve control anticipation. I retain the increased sensor size (0.016) and wheel track (0.16) to preserve noise robustness and turning stability. The controller parameters remain unchanged as they were already tuned to this geometry. I expect this incremental forward sensor shift to reduce line loss events, lower rms error, and decrease steering oscillations, leading to better progress and completion rates on both oval and s-bend tracks, thus improving generalization.
